questions.question: What does alcohol do?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain activity and reduces the skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must bear either right or left.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must bear either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must turn either right or left.

questions.question: What does alcohol cause?
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
When a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and when a traffic officer signals you to stop.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Use your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Sound your horn at passing motorists.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers and move as far off the road as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your vehicle is disabled.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn to catch your exit. Go to the next exit instead.

questions.question: Which statement about aggressive drivers is true?

options.text: They take out their frustrations on other motorists.
They run stop signs, speed, tailgate, weave through traffic, make unsafe lane changes, and honk unnecessarily.

questions.explanation: Aggressive drivers harass other people while breaking traffic laws. They run red lights and stop signs, speed, tailgate, weave in and out of traffic, make unsafe lane changes, and honk, gesture, or yell angrily.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.
It has no effect on judgment but harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reduces reaction time and vision. It also impairs your judgment of speed and distance, lowers your caution, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: Are drivers responsible for making sure children are properly secured in vehicles?
questions.explanation: Drivers must ensure that all passengers under 18 are properly secured with a seat belt, booster seat, or child safety seat, regardless of where they sit in the vehicle.

questions.question: What must you do before leaving your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle unattended, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing the radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers make 200 decisions for every mile driven. You must keep your full attention on driving. Any other activity can be dangerous.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes require you to change how you drive.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain and fog. Be aware of vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: What should you do to change lanes?

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, then change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal and check your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one is in the lane you want to enter. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol level (BAC)?

options.text: Let your body break down the alcohol over time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let your body break down the alcohol over time.
questions.explanation: Only time will lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers will not reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they cannot change your BAC.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection go first. You can continue, but drive at a speed that lets you stop if the light changes.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Stay out of traffic lanes to avoid being hit. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn you about hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They get you ready for road hazards. This sign tells you a stop sign is coming and you should be ready to stop.

questions.question: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when you need to react to other drivers' sudden movements.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when other drivers make unexpected moves.

questions.question: Driving involves risk, so it is smart to keep improving your driving and observation skills.
questions.explanation: Driving is unsafe if you think you have nothing to improve. Always work on improving your driving and observation skills for your safety and others' safety.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.
questions.explanation: Create a habit when getting in and out of your car. Before starting the engine, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: The most common mistake drivers make when backing up is not looking both ways behind them.
questions.explanation: The most common mistake when backing up is failing to look both ways behind the car. Mirrors do not show everything. Turn your body and head to the right and look through the rear window to see more.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving compared to other things?

options.text: It affects your driving the same way alcohol does.
It affects your driving the same way amphetamines do.
It affects your driving the same way anger does.
It affects your driving the same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects your driving the same way alcohol does.
questions.explanation: Tiredness and alcohol have the same effects on your driving. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving like having a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours impairs driving like having a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must do. When you see this sign, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who drank alcohol before driving?

options.text: They always know the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
They are better drivers because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your brain and body. It weakens judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time. Never drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This triangle-shaped sign means "Yield." When you see it, slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and other traffic cross first. Only stop if you need to.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Any eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop your car completely and look for pedestrians and other traffic. Wait until the intersection is clear before going forward.

questions.question: You cannot pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus with flashing red lights, you must stop before reaching it and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. On roads with a median or shared center lane, cars on the opposite side of the bus do not have to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic light is coming up ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on the hill ahead.
There are trucks on the hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill or downgrade is ahead.
